name: Jungle
notes: Dense, tangled seasonally-moist (monsoon) forest and rainforest edge: shorter canopy than true rainforest, thick bamboo and giant-herb understory, vines. Drawn on Indo-Burma monsoon forest, SE Asian secondary jungle, Amazon bamboo forest and Congo-margin secondary growth.

canopy.silhouette: tall straight dark bole, dense rounded crown

growth.juvenile_note: Seed germinates within days of falling at the start of the monsoon, sometimes still on the tree; 2 thick, unequal fleshy cotyledons, then broad shiny leaves. Young sal is famous for 'die-back': the shoot dies back to the ground in drought, frost or fire for several years while the taproot grows, then one shoot escapes and grows away as a straight whip. Coppices freely.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Database (up to 6 m at 6 yr, mature 18-32 m; fruits regularly from ~15 yr; seed dead within 2 weeks; needs much light; coppices); Troup, Silviculture of Indian Trees (seedling die-back; seedlings bear moderate shade); Wikipedia (to 40 m); lifespan estimated

fruiting.source: Atluri et al. 2004 Current Science (sal: explosive pollen release, wind pollination with insect visitors, mixed mating); ICRAF/Troup (creamy fragrant flowers in big panicles Feb-Apr; ovoid nut with 5 unequal wings to ~7 cm ripens May-June; good seed years every 3-5 yr); seeds pressed for sal butter and eaten as famine food

The sapling is a fast, straight whip with a four-angled stem and a few pairs of giant leaves, often several metres tall in 2-3 years, before it forks and spreads into a tall tree with a rounded crown.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (Tectona grandis: 13 m at 5 yr, 16.5 m at 10, 21.5 m at 20, up to 45 m at 80; first flowering usually at 8-10 yr; very strong light demander; rotation ~80 yr); Wikipedia Teak (germination 15-30 days after pretreatment; Kannimara teak ~47.5 m, 450-500 yr old).

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (flowers Jun-Sep in Thailand; fruit mature ~4 months after fertilisation, Nov-Jan; natural fruit set 0.5-5%; bees the main pollinators; hard woody fruit in an inflated bladder-like calyx, 1,000-3,500 fruits/kg); Wikipedia (panicles 25-40 cm of small white fragrant flowers; fruit 1.2-1.8 cm). growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds wait in the soil until a gap opens. The seedling's first leaves are small and simple or barely lobed; each new leaf is larger and more deeply cut until the huge umbrella-like palmate leaves (deep lobes, pale undersides) appear. It shoots up as an unbranched hollow pole topped by a tuft of big leaves, with stilt roots at the base, branching candelabra-like only later.

(C. obtusifolia demography: fast-growing gap pioneer); Vazquez-Yanes & Smith 1982 (light-triggered germination); Wikipedia Cecropia (germination needs full sun and fluctuating temperatures, seeds viable >5 yr in soil, 5-15 m); values estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Usually starts as a bird-dropped seed in the fork of a host tree or a wall: a small leafy sprig that sends thin roots down the host's trunk. Once the roots reach the soil they thicken and fuse, strangling the host, and the crown spreads; drooping aerial roots from the branches reach the ground and become pillar trunks, so one tree becomes a grove.
growth.source: Troup 1921 Silviculture of Indian Trees (hemi-epiphytic start, aerial roots becoming pillars); Wikipedia Ficus benghalensis. Ages estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Ficus benghalensis (paired axillary figs ripening red, pollinated by Eupristina masoni, eaten by birds, bats and monkeys); Troup 1921. Crop estimated.

shrub.name: Alocasia (Himalayan)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a single small heart-shaped leaf from a tiny corm, then a rosette of a few broad, wavy-edged, light green arrowhead leaves on long stalks whose lower parts clasp the stem. A short, thick, ringed stem rises after a few years and suckers around the base build clumps of big upright leaves in moist ravines and forest edges.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Alocasia odora: 0.5-1.6 m, corms 4-10 cm, petioles 0.3-1 m clasping the stem, ovate cordate light green leaves; night-scented flowers; raw tissue full of raphides) and Useful Tropical Plants (semi-shade, seed best sown fresh, germinates best at 24 C). Rates and ages estimated.

shrub.name: Wild banana

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: the first leaves are small, narrow and lance-shaped, rolled round one another into a short soft pseudostem. Each new leaf is broader until the plant is a small copy of the adult with a green, often dark-blotched pseudostem. Each pseudostem flowers once and dies; narrow-leaved 'sword suckers' rise from the rhizome to replace it, so the clump lives on for decades.
growth.source: ProMusa and Simmonds 'Bananas' (pseudostem fruits ~1-1.5 yr after emergence and then dies; suckers replace it; seeds of wild bananas germinate slowly and erratically over weeks to months); timings from seed estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Almost never grows from seed: it flowers rarely and sets virtually no seed, so new clumps start from culm or branch pieces (often river-borne) that root and sprout within weeks. A young clump is a few thin leafy shoots; each rainy season it sends up thicker culms until, after 3-7 years, full-size green or golden-striped culms 10-20 m tall shoot up in a couple of months.

Each rainy season the young clump sends up stouter culms than the year before, reaching full-size culms (up to ~30 m tall, 20-28 cm thick) after roughly a decade. New shoots are fat conical spears wrapped in large brown hairy sheaths that elongate up to 40 cm a day; culm branches and leaves appear only after the culm reaches full height.

growth.juvenile_note: Young plants appear 6-7 weeks after spores land on burnt or disturbed bare soil: the first fronds are small, simple and lobed, becoming finely divided and adult-like after about 18 weeks. epiphyte.name: Bird's nest fern

growth.juvenile_note: Spores germinate over 2-7 weeks into heart-shaped prothalli on wet bark and moss; 3-6 months after sowing tiny, simple, spoon- to strap-shaped, apple-green fronds appear. The young fern is a small open funnel of undivided glossy fronds with a dark midrib that widens year by year into a nest-like rosette catching leaf litter.
growth.source: Asplenium nidus developmental study (Am. J. Plant Sci., scirp.org): 47% of spores germinated by day 47, 100% by day 60, gametangia at 60-100 days; grower guides (Planet Natural); frond growth, first spores and lifespan estimated.

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

epiphyte.name: Climbing fern

growth.juvenile_note: Heart-shaped green gametophytes on moist soil; the sporeling's first leaves are tiny fan-shaped or two-lobed blades on hair-thin stalks, not climbing at all. Later fronds have a wiry rachis that twines up shrubs like a vine stem, bearing lacy, triangular, finely lobed pinnae; fertile pinnae with fringed, sporangia-bearing margins come higher up. Frost browns the fronds back to the rhizome.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Lygodium spp. review (gametophytes sexually mature within 5 wk of germination, sporophytes produced through week 12; fronds 1-30 m; killed by frost, dead fronds stay draped; fertile June-Sept in the Carolinas); Lott et al. 2003 Am. J. Bot. 90:1144 (reproductive biology); EPPO datasheet

epiphyte.name: Monstera

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings creep across the dark forest floor away from the light (skototropism) until they touch a tree trunk, then climb it. Juvenile leaves are small, entire and heart-shaped, often pressed flat against the bark like shingles; higher up the leaves get huge, deeply split and holed (fenestrated) on long stalks, and cord-like aerial roots dangle to the ground.
growth.source: Wikipedia Monstera deliciosa (seedlings grow towards darkness until they find a trunk; juvenile leaves entire, later lobed and fenestrate; climbs to 20 m; flowers ~3 yr after planting in ideal conditions); vine lifespan estimated

epiphyte.name: Staghorn fern

growth.juvenile_note: Spores give green heart-shaped prothalli on bark; the first sporophyte fronds are small, simple, spoon-shaped and felted with white star-hairs. Soon it forms round, flat shield fronds that clasp the branch (green, later brown and papery), from which grey-green, forked 'antler' fronds arch out; pups around it build a ball-shaped colony.
growth.source: Estimated from staghorn fern cultivation from spore (prothalli in weeks, first fronds after a few months, fertile antler fronds after several years) and the species' form as a clumping epiphyte of eastern Australian rainforest margins
